comments.author: @suzannepoole8617
comments.text:
This is not a pandemic type of virus. But it is a quarantine level virus because it does have a significant death rate and this particular strain is known to be person to person. And it's incubation is long, 1-8 weeks. And because a 3rd person beyond the couple died and several are sick, it's a mandatory quarantine situation. 
It's likely the couple contracted before boarding but the spread is curious.  Did they dance, kiss? The concern is airborne  or something else. 
I remember watching videos out of China in December 2019 and knew immediately their mystery disease was airborne. It was another 6 + months before our own government would say that. 
My suspicion is this may have some capability because it's respiratory impact causes coughing. 
And you don't need contact like touching mouse feces or urine.  You can contract it by inhaling contaminated dust particulate.  Which is why you should wear a mask or respirator if you have to clean up a nest or even food they've gotten into. 
I used to be a CDC officer at a regional health care center.  Not a doctor but was charged with reading all the alerts and journals, taught public health classes and worked directly with 26 different specialities. And my ex almost died after a business trip where  hanta was investigated. After a week of increasing illnessanda couple days in ICU, I suggested legionnaires which was later confirmed. 
Unfortunately for these passengers, it's best to quarantine them on the ship. Transferring them to a hotel could just contaminate another site and become very difficult to control. 
The unknown about transmission and long incubation is very challenging. Especially feeling imprisoned with a high fatality virus such as this. Estimated at 30%.  And I doubt there's much data as it's rare and situationally an even weirder aspect to have so many people in a confined environment. And it takes considerable amount of research to study the particular strain and particulars of mobility, etc.
Personally, I would never go on a cruise. I caught norovirus that ran rapid in my community from a school outbreak. The only public place I went that week was a solo lunch. But it can be transmitted by touching a surface.   The entire school system had to shutdown for a couple weeks and buildings decontaminated. I was brutally ill for days and had to cancel a holiday.
